problem: Worn seat washer and stem O-ring
summary: The spout keeps dripping while the handle is closed, and water seeps out around the handle base. Both point to a worn rubber seat washer and a cracked stem O-ring inside the compression stem. This is a classic 20-minute fix.

markers.label: Spout drips while closed
markers.detail: Steady drip with the handle off: the seat washer no longer seals.

markers.label: Cracked O-ring at handle base
markers.detail: The seal ring under the handle is cracked, so water escapes around the stem.

markers.label: Water tracking down the body
markers.detail: Seepage runs down both sides of the valve body and leaves mineral scale.

markers.label: Shutoff valves found
markers.detail: Both supply valves are reachable, so you can do this without shutting off the whole house.

steps.title: Shut off the water
steps.detail: Turn both shutoff valves under the sink clockwise until they stop. Open the faucet to drain the line.

steps.title: Remove the handle
steps.detail: Pry off the H cap, undo the screw underneath, and lift the handle straight up.

steps.title: Unscrew the stem
steps.detail: Hold the faucet body and turn the stem nut counterclockwise with an adjustable wrench. Lift out the stem.

steps.title: Swap the seat washer
steps.detail: Remove the brass screw at the bottom of the stem, replace the rubber washer with the same size from the kit, and put the screw back.

steps.title: Replace the O-ring
steps.detail: Roll off the cracked O-ring, fit the new one, and coat it lightly with plumber's grease.

steps.title: Reassemble and test
steps.detail: Screw the stem back in snugly, refit the handle, turn the water on slowly, and check the spout for drips.
